title: The stratum bound with rational coefficients
statement:
Work in the standing scheme and coefficient setting of [det-uniform-constructible-ext-torsion]. Let $a:S\hookrightarrow X$ be locally closed, $\Lambda=E$ or $\Qlb$, and $L$ a lisse $\Lambda_S$-module. Lower shriek is closed direct image after open extension by zero. Ext means Hom to a shift in $D(X_{\mathrm{proét}},\Lambda)$ [def-pc-ext].

For $\Lambda=E$, put $E_0=E$ and $L^{(0)}=L$. For $\Lambda=\Qlb$, fix a finite $E_0/\mathbf Q_\ell$ and a lisse $E_{0,S}$-module $L^{(0)}$ with $(L^{(0)})_{\Qlb}\simeq L$, as supplied by [sk-thm-sfb-qlbar-two-colimit](1). Choose once and for all a finite stratification of $X$, adapted to the constructible sheaf $a_!L^{(0)}$ [sk-def-sfb-constructible], refining $S$ and its complement, ordered with successive unions open as in [det-lem-coefficient-heart-common-stratification](1). Its strata inside $S$, denoted $S_k$, have lisse $\mathcal O_{E_0}$-lattices in $L^{(0)}|_{S_k}$, as in [sk-lem-stratified-lattice]. Such an ordered refinement exists. Write $a_k:S_k\hookrightarrow X$ as $S_k\hookrightarrow Z_k\hookrightarrow X$, open followed by closed, with $Z_k=\overline{S_k}$, and let $j_k:X\setminus Z_k\hookrightarrow X$. Put
$$
c_{a_k}=\operatorname{cd}_\ell(j_k)+\operatorname{cd}_\ell(S_k)+2,\qquad
 d_{a,L}=\max\bigl(\{0\}\cup\{c_{a_k}\}_k\bigr).
$$
Then, for every locally closed $b:T\hookrightarrow X$ and every lisse $\Lambda_T$-module $M$,
$$
\Ext^q_\Lambda(a_!L,b_!M)=0\qquad(q>d_{a,L}).
$$
The chosen finite coefficient model and source stratification, and hence $d_{a,L}$, are independent of $b,M$. Cohomological dimensions have the extended nonnegative-integer convention of [det-uniform-constructible-ext-torsion]; an infinite cutoff gives a vacuous bound. For an empty source take $d_{a,L}=0$.

If $\Lambda=E$ and $L$ has a lisse $\mathcal O_E$-lattice $L_0\hookrightarrow L$ on all of $S$, the same Ext conclusion holds with the original factorization $a=i\circ u:S\hookrightarrow Z\hookrightarrow X$ and cutoff $c_a=\operatorname{cd}_\ell(j)+\operatorname{cd}_\ell(S)+2$: for every locally closed $b:T\hookrightarrow X$, every lisse $\Lambda_T$-module $M$, and every $q>c_a$, $\Ext^q_\Lambda(a_!L,b_!M)=0$. The analogous assertion holds for $\Qlb$ when the chosen finite model $L^{(0)}$ has a lisse $\mathcal O_{E_0}$-lattice on all of $S$. In general the bound proved after refining the source is the maximum of its refined-stratum cutoffs, with no assertion that it equals $c_a$.

proof.text: We first check the constructibility required below, for either rational coefficient ring. The standing schemes $X,S,T$ are Noetherian: apply [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian] over $\operatorname{Spec}k$, whose field has no ideals other than $0$ and $k$. For any locally closed $h:W\hookrightarrow X$ and lisse $P$ on $W$, factor $h=i\circ u$ through its closure. All open immersions in this Noetherian situation are quasi-compact. Parts (1),(2),(4) of [det-sf-open-closed-sequence-ring-sheaf] show that $h_!P=i_*u_!P$ restricts to $P$ on $W$ and to zero on the two complementary pieces $\overline W\setminus W$ and $X\setminus\overline W$: for the first piece, the base-changed open immersion is empty; for the second, the base-changed closed immersion is empty. Both functors are exact. On $W$ a lisse sheaf has the finite constant local model given by its finite free local bases, and the zero sheaf has the zero model. Thus these three locally closed pieces form an adapted stratification under [sk-def-sfb-constructible]. In degree zero, $h_!P$ is bounded and has only this constructible cohomology sheaf; hence $h_!P\in\Dbc(X,\Lambda)$ by that same definition. This applies to all finite-field models $a_!L_E,b_!M_E$ later used in the Hom-colimit theorem.

source.place: Preparation for both coefficient paragraphs: Noetherian hypotheses and bounded constructible lower-shriek models

proof.text: Take $\Lambda=E$. Apply [sk-lem-stratified-lattice] to $L$ on $S$ and choose its finite lattice stratification before any target is chosen; no extension $E'/E$ is required. Extend the partition to $X$ by the two complementary pieces in Step 1, then apply [det-lem-coefficient-heart-common-stratification](1) to obtain a finite ordered refinement. A lattice stays lisse on a further stratum: base change its free local cover, where its restriction is $\mathcal O_E^{\oplus r}$ and still localizes to the restricted $L$. Denote the resulting source strata by $S_k$ and their embeddings in $X$ by $a_k$, and define $c_{a_k}$ and $d_{a,L}$ only now, using these strata and their own closures and complements. By [det-lem-coefficient-heart-filtration], applied directly on $X$ to $C=a_!L$, this ordered adapted stratification gives a finite filtration of $C$ whose nonzero graded pieces are $C_k=a_{k,!}(L|_{S_k})$; the complementary pieces contribute zero. For any target $b_!M$, independently apply the lattice theorem on $T$ and ordered-refinement theorem on $X$ to its partition and complement, and apply the filtration theorem to $N=b_!M$. Its nonzero graded pieces are $N_t=b_{t,!}(M|_{T_t})$, each with a lisse lattice. The source partition is unchanged by this target preparation. If $L$ has a global lattice, omit the source filtration entirely and keep $C=a_!L$ with its original factorization and cutoff $c_a$.

source.place: Coefficients E, opening lattice and refinement paragraph; corrected source cutoff

proof.text:
Fix a source piece $C_k=a_{k,!}L_k$ and target piece $N_t=b_{t,!}M_t$ from Step 2, with lisse $\mathcal O_E$-lattices $L_{k,0},M_{t,0}$. In the global-source-lattice case use $a,L_0$ instead. Put $A=a_{k,!}L_{k,0}$ and $B=b_{t,!}M_{t,0}$. The localization and flatness statement [det-prop-sfb-qlbar-colimit-x-invert-ell] applies on $X$ and on both strata. Hence derived scalar extension agrees with ordinary tensor with $E$. Clause (2) of [det-prop-scalar-six-pullback] identifies $A_E=C_k$, $B_E=N_t$. The derived adjunction in [sk-def-sfb-coefficient-change] therefore gives
$$
\Ext_E^q(C_k,N_t)\cong\operatorname{Hom}_{D(X_{\mathrm{proét}},\mathcal O_E)}(A,\operatorname{Res}_{E/\mathcal O_E}(E_X\otimes B)[q]).
$$

source.place: Coefficients E: flat localization, scalar/lower-shriek comparison and derived adjunction

proof.text:
The ring-module telescope in [det-prop-sfb-qlbar-colimit-x-invert-ell], tensored with $B$, is still colimiting by [lem-pc-module-filtered-colimits-tensor], in degree zero on the pro-étale site (taken small in the sheaf universe). Since $\mathcal O_{E,X}\otimes B=B$ and its transition $\ell\otimes1$ is multiplication by $\ell$, this gives
$$
\operatorname{Res}_{E/\mathcal O_E}(E_X\otimes B)\cong\varinjlim(B\xrightarrow{\ell}B\xrightarrow{\ell}\cdots).
$$
The leg at $n$ is $m\mapsto\ell^{-n}m$, and compatibility is $\ell^{-(n+1)}\ell m=\ell^{-n}m$. This is a sheaf-module colimit; no objectwise colimit assertion is used.

source.place: Coefficients E: target localization as the tensor of the coefficient telescope

proof.text:
The telescope index is the small filtered category $\mathbf N$ and all its complexes have the common termwise lower bound $0$. Its source $A=a_{k,!}L_{k,0}$ has a finite locally free integral lattice. Thus the integral clause of [sk-lem-constructible-ext-continuity], applied to Step 4's telescope and Step 3's adjunction, gives
$$
\Ext_E^q(C_k,N_t)\cong\varinjlim_n\Ext^q_{\mathcal O_E}(a_{k,!}L_{k,0},b_{t,!}M_{t,0}),
$$
with transitions induced by multiplication by $\ell$ on the target. The integral bound [det-uniform-constructible-ext-integral] kills every term for $q>c_{a_k}$: the standing setting and closed/open factorization are unchanged, and both lattices are lisse. Consequently $\Ext_E^q(C_k,N_t)=0$ in that range, independently of $t$. With a global source lattice the same calculation uses the original $a$ and gives $q>c_a$.

source.place: Coefficients E: integral-source continuity and the integral bound

proof.text: Fix $k$. In the target filtration of Step 2, [lem-sc-abelian-ext-covariant-exact] gives the exact segment $\Ext^q(C_k,N_{t-1})\to\Ext^q(C_k,N_t^{\mathrm{fil}})\to\Ext^q(C_k,N_t^{\mathrm{fil}}/N_{t-1})$. Induct on $t$ for each $q>c_{a_k}$: at $t=0$ Ext into zero is zero by additivity [def-pc-ext], and at the next stage the two end groups vanish by induction and Step 5. Hence $\Ext^q(C_k,b_!M)=0$ for $q>c_{a_k}$. Next fix $q>d_{a,L}$ and induct along the source filtration $C_s^{\mathrm{fil}}$. The exact segment from [lem-coef-ext-contravariant-six-term] is $\Ext^q(C_s^{\mathrm{fil}}/C_{s-1}^{\mathrm{fil}},b_!M)\to\Ext^q(C_s^{\mathrm{fil}},b_!M)\to\Ext^q(C_{s-1}^{\mathrm{fil}},b_!M)$. Again its end groups vanish, by the preceding target induction and the source induction hypothesis. The zero-source base case follows from additivity. This proves the $E$ conclusion with the maximum of the $c_{a_k}$, not the cutoff of the original unrefined $a$. If the source has a global lattice, only the target induction is needed and it retains the original $c_a$. An infinite cutoff leaves no $q$ to check; the empty source is zero.

source.place: Opening refinement paragraph: the two finite-filtration inductions, with corrected maximum

proof.text:
For $\Lambda=\Qlb$, clause (1) of [sk-thm-sfb-qlbar-two-colimit] gives a finite $E_0$ and lisse model $L^{(0)}$ for $L$. Fix $C_0=a_!L^{(0)}$ and the source lattice partition of Step 2 before choosing any target. Steps 3–6 prove its $E_0$ bound $d_{a,L}$ against every lower-shriek lisse $E_0$-target. For a given $M$, clause (1) on $T$ gives a finite-field model; a common finite extension $E\supset E_0$ contains that field. Put $C_E=(C_0)_E=a_!L_E$, $N_E=b_!M_E$. Clauses (2),(3) of [det-prop-scalar-six-pullback] identify their $\Qlb$ extensions with $a_!L,b_!M$. Their lisse restrictions and zero complements place $C_E,N_E$ in $\Dbc(X,E)$ by Step 1. Clause (2) of the two-colimit theorem therefore gives
$$
\Ext^q_{\Qlb}(a_!L,b_!M)\cong\varinjlim_{F\supset E}\operatorname{Hom}_{D(X_{\mathrm{proét}},F)}((C_0)_F,(N_E)_F[q]).
$$

source.place: Coefficients Qbar: fixed finite source model and bounded-constructible Hom colimit

proof.text:
For any finite $F\supset E$, factor $b=i\circ u$ with $u$ open and $i$ closed. Apply [def-sfb-comap-lower-star-iso] to $i$ and [def-sfb-comap-open-immersion-shriek-iso] to $u$, both with the condensed coefficient inclusion $E_0\to F$. Composing their module-object isomorphisms gives
$$
\operatorname{Res}_{F/E_0}(b_!M_F)\cong b_!(\operatorname{Res}_{F/E_0}M_F).
$$
Thus lower-shriek restriction of scalars is supplied by existing comparison nodes, including the coefficient actions, rather than an identification of underlying sheaves alone. Restriction is exact by [sk-def-sfb-change-of-scalars](4), so these isomorphisms also apply to the degree-zero derived objects.

source.place: Coefficients Qbar: restriction through the two locally closed lower-shriek factors

proof.text:
The sheaf $M_F$ is lisse: tensor its finite free $E$-local models with $F$, using the flat scalar extension of [lem-sfb-subfield-flat]. On a cover trivializing it as $F^{\oplus r}$, the finite-free coefficient comparison [det-prop-sfb-cartesian-coefficients-finite-free] for $E_0\subset F$ gives
$$
\operatorname{Res}_{F/E_0}M_F\cong E_0^{\oplus r[F:E_0]}.
$$
That comparison is compatible with inverse image, so it applies on the members of this pro-étale covering. This proves that the restricted target is lisse over $E_0$, with finite rank even when ranks vary between members.

source.place: Coefficients Qbar: finite free local models after restriction

proof.text:
By [det-prop-scalar-six-pullback](2),(3), $(N_E)_F=b_!M_F$ and $(C_E)_F=(C_0)_F$. The derived scalar adjunction [sk-def-sfb-coefficient-change] for $E_0\to F$ identifies each term of Step 7's Hom colimit with
$$
\Ext^q_{E_0}(C_0,\operatorname{Res}_{F/E_0}(b_!M_F))
\cong\Ext^q_{E_0}(C_0,b_!(\operatorname{Res}_{F/E_0}M_F)),
$$
where Step 8 supplies the second isomorphism. By Step 9 this is a lisse $E_0$-target. The $E_0$ bound from Steps 3–6 annihilates it for $q>d_{a,L}$. Every term of the colimit is zero, so the colimit is zero. The source partition and cutoff were fixed before $b,M,F$ and have not changed. If the finite source model has a lattice on all of $S$, Step 6 gives its bound with $c_a$ instead; the same termwise argument kills this colimit for $q>c_a$.

source.place: Coefficients Qbar: scalar adjunction and termwise fixed-source vanishing

statement_change.old_statement:
Work in the standing scheme and coefficient setting of [det-uniform-constructible-ext-torsion]. Let $a:S\hookrightarrow X$ be locally closed, $\Lambda=E$ or $\Qlb$, and $L$ a lisse $\Lambda_S$-module. Lower shriek is closed direct image after open extension by zero. Ext means Hom to a shift in $D(X_{\mathrm{proét}},\Lambda)$ [def-pc-ext].

For $\Lambda=E$, put $E_0=E$ and $L^{(0)}=L$. For $\Lambda=\Qlb$, fix a finite $E_0/\mathbf Q_\ell$ and a lisse $E_{0,S}$-module $L^{(0)}$ with $(L^{(0)})_{\Qlb}\simeq L$, as supplied by [sk-thm-sfb-qlbar-two-colimit](1). Choose once and for all a finite stratification of $X$, adapted to the constructible sheaf $a_!L^{(0)}$ [sk-def-sfb-constructible], refining $S$ and its complement, ordered with successive unions open as in [det-lem-coefficient-heart-common-stratification](1). Its strata inside $S$, denoted $S_k$, have lisse $\mathcal O_{E_0}$-lattices in $L^{(0)}|_{S_k}$, as in [sk-lem-stratified-lattice]. Such an ordered refinement exists. Write $a_k:S_k\hookrightarrow X$ as $S_k\hookrightarrow Z_k\hookrightarrow X$, open followed by closed, with $Z_k=\overline{S_k}$, and let $j_k:X\setminus Z_k\hookrightarrow X$. Put
$$
c_{a_k}=\operatorname{cd}_\ell(j_k)+\operatorname{cd}_\ell(S_k)+2,\qquad
 d_{a,L}=\max\bigl(\{0\}\cup\{c_{a_k}\}_k\bigr).
$$
Then, for every locally closed $b:T\hookrightarrow X$ and every lisse $\Lambda_T$-module $M$,
$$
\Ext^q_\Lambda(a_!L,b_!M)=0\qquad(q>d_{a,L}).
$$
The chosen finite coefficient model and source stratification, and hence $d_{a,L}$, are independent of $b,M$. Cohomological dimensions have the extended nonnegative-integer convention of [det-uniform-constructible-ext-torsion]; an infinite cutoff gives a vacuous bound. For an empty source take $d_{a,L}=0$.

If $\Lambda=E$ and $L$ already has a lisse $\mathcal O_E$-lattice on all of $S$, the same conclusion holds with $d_{a,L}=c_a=\operatorname{cd}_\ell(j)+\operatorname{cd}_\ell(S)+2$ for the original factorization $a=i\circ u:S\hookrightarrow Z\hookrightarrow X$ and $j:X\setminus Z\hookrightarrow X$. The analogous assertion holds for $\Qlb$ if the chosen finite model has a lattice on all of $S$. In general the bound proved after refining the source is the maximum of its refined-stratum cutoffs, with no assertion that it equals $c_a$.
statement_change.what: The final global-lattice clause incorrectly made the stratum cutoff d equal to c_a and used an arbitrary lisse module as the antecedent. The source requires a lisse O_E-lattice inclusion on all of S (or on the fixed finite Qbar model) and concludes the Ext vanishing above c_a. The cutoff d is the maximum only over strata contained in the source; the prior Lean rendering also omitted the source/complement refinement, ordered-open data, lattice data, and fixed finite model data.
